errors.english: The definition of the state of the general principal
errors.why: After the sentence finishing from the previous side, the Tibetan says 'Therefore it is not entirely unseen. If you accept that, then here this is contradictory. If you wonder what contradicts it: "guṇa" and so on' — none of this is translated.

fix.find: The definition of the state of the general principal
fix.replace: Therefore it is not the case that it is never seen at all. If you accept this, then here this is contradictory. If you wonder what contradicts it: "guṇa" and so on. The definition of the state of the general principal

errors.english: is the (pradhana) primary matter which is also extremely hollow and devoid of intrinsic nature
errors.why: The verse says that what has entered the path of vision is extremely hollow, and so the pradhāna too becomes hollow; the English instead identifies visible things such as gardens with the pradhāna.

note: The Sāṃkhya argument is mostly followed, but the opening sentences of the side are skipped and the cited verse is construed so that visible things are identified with the pradhāna.

errors.english: which can give off smoke-like vapour
errors.why: The verse names only śakramūrdhan; the explanation that it gives off smoke-like vapour is interpretation inserted into the verse without being marked as a note.

note: A faithful rendering of the svabhāva/kārya-hetu argument and its summary verses; the only problem is a small unmarked gloss inside the verse.
Accurate rendering of the word-by-word commentarial glosses on the verses about skill in speech.

errors.english: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena that are incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,
errors.why: The Tibetan says right view and the rest are cultivated as the antidote that ABANDONS non-virtuous dharmas such as wrong view, not something that counteracts their abandonment.

fix.find: to counteract the abandonment of non-virtuous phenomena that are incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,
fix.replace: as the antidote that abandons non-virtuous phenomena incompatible with liberation, such as wrong views,

errors.english: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
errors.why: 'Noble, supramundane' (āryā lokottarā) describes right view itself; it is not in the list of objects of wrong views, which begins with 'self'.

fix.find: It is that which is not motivated by views of a noble being, a worldly being, a self,
fix.replace: It is the noble, supramundane view that is not motivated by views of a self,

errors.why: In the triad virtuous / non-virtuous / (a)vyākṛta this is the ethically determined (or indeterminate) category, not 'prophesied'.

note: The Akṣayamati citation and the discussion of vāsanā are mostly sound, but the opening sentence reverses the antidote relation and the sūtra's definition of right view is mis-segmented.

errors.english: then it would follow that the sensory faculties themselves are gradually produced
errors.why: The consequence is that the I-cognition would be produced, mediately, by the sense faculties; it is not that the faculties are produced.

fix.find: then it would follow that the sensory faculties themselves are gradually produced
fix.replace: then it would follow that this cognition is, mediately, produced by the sensory faculties

errors.english: it is not neither the sensory faculties nor the cognition produced by them
errors.why: The Tibetan says the I-cognition determines only the self and NOT the faculties or the cognition they produce; the double negative says the opposite.

fix.find: it is not neither the sensory faculties nor the cognition produced by them
fix.replace: it determines neither the sensory faculties nor the cognition produced by them

errors.english: Furthermore, through the very cause of the sensory faculties, one understands that in the stages of fetal development
errors.why: This is an alternative explanation: the cause of the faculties is understood to be the mental consciousness, either in the embryo (nur nur po etc.) or in the previous life, and not the elements. The English garbles who causes what.

errors.english: how could it follow what is seen by the senses? It is only that which arises gradually from the senses.
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར here is explanatory: since it follows what the faculties have seen, it too arises mediately from the faculties. It is a consequence, not a rhetorical question.

note: The first half, on the faculties and the other world, is serviceable, but the closing argument about the I-cognition is misconstrued in several places.

errors.why: This is a Mūlasarvāstivāda text, so the Sanskrit saṃghāvaśeṣa is meant, not the Pali saṅghādisesa.

errors.english: He must be mindful and remain very composed.
errors.why: The reciter must have the Prātimokṣa text thoroughly settled (mastered), not 'remain composed'.

note: A clear and accurate account of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's and elder's duties; it has small terminological slips.

errors.english: how does an understanding arise regarding the negation of the meaning of words as exclusion from things other than those non-exclusions?
errors.why: The question is how, from words and so on that are NOT other-exclusion (anyāpoha), a cognition can arise that negates exclusion as word-meaning; 'gzhan sel ba' is misread as 'from things other than'.

note: The apoha discussion and the point about isolated words such as 'prameya' are rendered competently, with one garbled question.

errors.why: ཚང here is 'nest'; the gloss continues on the next side with 'is a dwelling (gnas)'.

errors.english: "You and the cowherd will come to know it through Śiva
errors.why: ཞི་བ appears to be Śivā, the cowherd's mother (བ་ལང་སྐྱོང་གི་མ), the woman whose hand throws the curd pot, not the god Śiva as an instrument.

note: Generally accurate glosses on the Vinayavastu narrative, with one mistranslated lemma and an uncertain reading of the Śivā episode, which the translator flags.

errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, so the Sanskrit jñaptidvitīya-karman is meant. The same Pali-for-Sanskrit substitution occurs in (ñatti) and (ñatticatuttha-kamma).

note: The rule that a karman counts as done once most of its final recitation is spoken, and the Upāli citation on boundary-setting, are rendered correctly. The only problem is Pali labels on Mūlasarvāstivāda terms.

errors.english: Therefore, a single cognition does not possess multiple referents,
errors.why: The verse affirms that a single cognition HAS many objects; the negation is added.

fix.find: Therefore, a single cognition does not possess multiple referents,
fix.replace: Therefore, a single cognition has multiple referents,

errors.english: Diverse impressions are not blended by the intellect,
errors.why: The verse says the cognition of the variegated (citra-buddhi) is not a blending of what is apprehended in succession; 'variegated' qualifies the cognition, not impressions that the intellect blends.

errors.english: It is because that very object was grasped
errors.why: ཡུལ here is 'place': the opponent says the colours are grasped in the same location, and the reply speaks of grasping in that place.

note: The refutation of the Vaiśeṣika account of variegated cognition is largely followed, but the concluding verse is negated and two steps of the argument are misconstrued.
